messages.author: 1220f7a833c6ec8b
messages.subject: Speed up tryallpositions()
parts:
Hi everyone!

I'm constructing a linkage map from NGS data and I'm trying to add in a few extra markers. To that end: is there a good way to make "tryallpositions()" faster? I'd love to do something like try a small sample of the positions (I have a lot of markers, so every fifth or tenth place to start with) and then try every single position in a reduced window of the chromosome. 

Thanks!

Joanna

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Speed up tryallpositions()
parts:
You could try using a very small number of iterations to get an initial understanding of location. For example, maxit=2.

But I'd be inclined to do a separate calculation that looks for association between the new markers and all available ones...even treating a new marker as a binary phenotype and doing a quick genome scan.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Speed up tryallpositions()
parts:
Hi Joanna,
I have had great luck with Karl's second approach - treating the marker as a binary trait and running scanone. I usually do this, place the new marker at the peak LOD position, then run ripple with a small window to see if it actually fits better in another spot. This approach is parallelizable - I have done it with 10k's of markers. 
Good luck,
John

messages.author: 04e62c3b36bb17bf
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Speed up tryallpositions()
parts:
Hi Joanna - that's exactly what I have used it for. 
I parallelize by chromosome, which speeds things up considerably. However, with lots of markers it does get really slow (because of the ripple step). The general pipeline is below. If you don't need the positions to be super precise and you already have a good linkage map, you can just do the scanone step, which is very fast and doesn't require parallelization. 
Good luck,
John

### Step 1: Add all markers into a phenotype matrix
cross$pheno<-data.frame(new.markers.coded.as.numeric)

### Step 2: Figure out the linkage group of all markers
s1s<-scanone(cross, pheno.col = all.your.marker.names)
chrs<-sapply(all.your.marker.names, function(x) s1$chr[which.max(s1[,x])])

### Step 3: set up your preferred parallelization - foreach, mclapply, .... Use unique(chrs) as the iterator. 
### Step 4: Find position of best marker
best.pos<-max(scanone(cross, pheno.col = marker1))$pos
### Step 5: Add marker based on its peak position
cross<-addmarker(cross,...)
### Step 6: Ripple... i use qtlTools::repRipple, which switches marker order to the best automatically. Set window small... <=4.
cross<-repRipple(cross, chr = chr.of.best.peak)
